themeVerdicts.explanation: The Empire State Building is a landmark skyscraper with individually named public observatories on the 86th and 102nd floors, a fixed visitor entrance, and regularly operating public admission in New York City.
Top of the Rock is a named public observation deck with multiple elevated viewing levels in 30 Rockefeller Plaza, a high-rise in New York City.
One World Observatory is a named, ticketed public observation venue on floors 100–102 of One World Trade Center, with an exact visitor facility in New York City.
Edge is a named, regularly ticketed observation deck on the 100th floor of 30 Hudson Yards, with a fixed public entrance in New York City.
SUMMIT One Vanderbilt is a permanent, named public observation experience on the upper floors of the One Vanderbilt skyscraper, offering panoramic views from a fixed visitor facility.
Skydeck Chicago is a named public observation deck on the 103rd floor of Willis Tower, a high-rise in Chicago, with fixed visitor access.
360 Chicago is a named public observation venue on the 94th floor of 875 North Michigan Avenue, providing panoramic views from a fixed high-rise facility.

clueVerdicts.explanation: The clue's 1962 World's Fair completion, 605-foot height, 520-foot observation deck, and 41-second elevator ride uniquely identify the Space Needle.
The 128-story, 632-meter height, floors 118 and 119 observation decks, and 20.5-meter-per-second elevator record identify Shanghai Tower.
The world's-largest-frame description, dimensions, Zabeel Park setting, and contrasting old and new Dubai views identify Dubai Frame.
The indoor 360-degree deck on the 100th floor, 60-second lift journey from the second floor, and April 2011 opening identify Sky100.
The 102-story Art Deco design, 1930–31 construction, 1,250-foot roof height, and 86th- and 102nd-floor observatories identify the Empire State Building Observatory.
